data.name: Rem
data.gender_notes: Rem is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Greek mythology, Remus was a twin brother of Romulus, the legendary founder of Rome. The name Rem means 'obliterate' or 'erase'. In the Bible, Rem is not found as a personal name but is mentioned in Numbers 1:18 and 1 Chronicles 7:27 in relation to the tribe of Reuben. The name Rem carries the meaning “Obliterate, erase” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Rem usually hope their child will grow to embody obliterate, erase and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the power to overcome adversity and start anew.
data.etymology: Rem belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Obliterate, erase.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Rem total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

data.cultural_impact: The name Rem can be seen as a call to action, urging us to eliminate negative influences in our lives and make a positive impact on the world. In a broader sense, it could represent the removing of obstacles or challenges that hinder personal growth and progress.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Rem can be seen as a reminder of the importance of spiritual purification and the need to eliminate negative emotions and thoughts from our lives. It can also symbolize the elimination of sin and the pursuit of holiness and righteousness. Ultimately, the name Rem encourages us to strive for spiritual growth and transformation, erasing the old and making way for the new.
